newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Ten killed in Colombian "terrorist" bombing.
newsitem.headline: Ten killed in Colombian "terrorist" bombing.

text.p: A powerful bomb blast tore through a town in Colombia's notoriously violent northwest banana-growing region of Uraba on Thursday, killing at least 10 people and leaving nearly 50 injured, authorities said.
Army commander Gen. Manuel Jose Bonett, who blamed the bombing on leftist guerrillas, called it "an act of war" and the government repudiated it in a statement as a "treacherous terrorist attack."

The death toll from the morning blast was initially set at seven. But police and municipal officials in the bloodied town of Apartado raised it to 10 after rescue workers pulled the bodies of two men and a woman from the rubble of a hotel that was leveled in the explosion.

The town's acting mayor, Omar Largo Penilla, told national radio at least one other person was missing in the gutted remains of the four-story El Pescador Hotel and that the number of fatalities was likely to climb to at least 11.
The dead included a 3-year-old child and a policeman and Largo said 49 people were injured.
Police sources told Reuters the bomb -- which exploded in the back of a pickup truck at about 8:50 a.m. (1350 GMT) -- was believed to have been comprised of up to 220 pounds (100 kg) of dynamite.
Apart from the hotel eight other buildings, including the town's police headquarters, suffered serious structural damage and Largo said damages were estimated at more than $1.5 million.

At least six guerrillas died in a firefight with the military on Sunday in Uraba and regional military commander Gen. Ivan Ramirez said the truck bomb was to avenge both the deaths and the army's recent dismantling of several rebel encampments in Uraba.
"It was a retaliation by the FARC," said Ramirez, referring to leftist Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia rebels. "It's confirmed that it was them and carried out by their militias."

The vehicle the bomb exploded in had been rented by the town government for use as a garbage truck, according to Ramirez. He said it was hijacked by suspected guerrillas at about 7 a.m., laden with the dynamite, and then parked along the town's main street, about 65 feet (20 meters) from the police station.

Gunmen of the left and right have killed with impunity throughout Uraba for more than a decade. Guerrillas and right- wing paramilitary groups based in the impoverished region, on the Caribbean coast near Colombia's border with Panama, have long been known to control lucrative arms and drug smuggling routes.

In violence elsewhere in Colombia, authorities said two policemen were killed and four others were wounded in an overnight attack by about 200 FARC rebels on the small town of Labranzagrande in the Cordillera Oriental mountains of central Boyaca province.

The town's 14-strong police force held off the rebels, who launched their attack around midnight, until army reinforcements forced them to retreat into the surrounding mountains shortly after dawn, police said.
The police headquarters was totally destroyed and a cook working inside the headquarters was wounded in the fighting after she took up a rifle to back the police.
The FARC, Colombia's largest and oldest guerrilla group, was founded as a Marxist-led, pro-Soviet group in 1964.
